pcs/templar.html.title: Templar
pcs/templar.html.description: Infobox Infobox Powers: Killshot - Mastery: 0 1 SP: Hit a target with no roll, regardless of the situation. 2 SP: Hit 1D8 targets with a single motion and no roll. 3 SP: Drop a single target to 0 HP with a DEX roll. Super Senses - Mastery: +1 1 SP: Enhanced sensory abilities over a range of 5 miles. 2 SP: Discern detailed information from touching a surface, person, or object. Lucky - Mastery: 0 1 SP: Re-roll of any roll -- ATTEMPT or EFFORT. Effort: Basic (Weapons): 1 Tools: Guns: 3 Energy & Magic: Ultimate: Properties: Ammo for Days War Zone Super Car Loot: Arcane Cartridge Equipment: Micro Comms Thumper Pistol Team Suit +1 Def. 10/12 exploding bullets: deliver ultimate effort Background: Descendent of Timothy Murphy -- American sniper in the Revolutionary War. U.S. Army Ranger Sniper, DoD Military Experiment, and Super Soldier. Left the army after a psychotic break during a covert op involving civilians. Moved to Kansas City to disappear and start over. Recruited into Veritas Aeterna while seeking counseling and absolution. The Order of Eternal Truth: Papal bull Lux in Tenebris (Light in Darkness) established Ordo Veritas Aeterna (the Order of Eternal Truth). The Order was established as a response to the current challenging times, ordained to bring light, guidance, and protection where it is most needed. Lux in Tenebris is seen as a pivotal declaration, empowering and legitimizing the order's sacred duty to act as guardians of the faith and warriors of light amidst the darkness of the world.Hierarchy: Ordo Veritas Aeterna (Order of Eternal Truth): The overarching order dedicated to uncovering, protecting, and preserving divine truths. This order serves as the spiritual and ideological foundation for all its members and their actions. It is the modern incarnation of the Knights Templar. Militis Lucis Divinae (Knights of the Divine Light): The militant arm of the Veritas Aeterna. It is composed of knights and warriors who actively defend the order's principles and take on missions that require martial prowess. They are the protectors of the faith, ensuring that the divine mission is upheld through strength and valor. Umbrae Custos Divinae (Guardian Shadows of the Divine): A clandestine unit within the Militis Lucis Divinae, specializing in stealth, espionage, and assassination. This elite group operates in the shadows to carry out the most sensitive and critical missions that require a discreet touch or direct action against threats to the order. Bellator Umbrae (Warrior of the Shadow): A member of the Umbrae Custos Divinae, a "Shadow Warrior" skilled in the arts of stealth, combat, and strategy. These individuals are the unseen defenders of the order, executing tasks that require a blend of martial skill and clandestine operation.

pcs/the-green-knight.html.title: The Green Knight
pcs/the-green-knight.html.description: Infobox Infobox Powers: Armatura Dei (Armor of God): 0 SP: Immunity to Bullets 0 SP: +4 to DEF already added into score - Stealth rolls are HARD Shield of Faith - Mastery: 0 2 SP (Unyielding Aegis): Make a Str roll to prevent all damage from a ranged or melee attack that hits the hero.  The roll can be made as a reaction after the damage is inflicted to eliminate the damage.  This does not count against the number of actions the character takes per turn and can be used multiple times in the same turn.  This does not work against Area Effects.  The Green Knight may still suffer Knockback from an attack even though damage was prevented. 3 SP (Brother’s Guard): Damage Deflection with Shield: 3 SP, same as above but eliminate the damage from an attack against another person.  The Green Knight must be within NEAR of that person.  This does not count as an action. Smite (Martial Arts): 1 SP: EASY Str roll to inflict 1d6 +3 + 1d12 damage on an attack.  Melee weapons only. Flight (from armor): 1 SP: Perform a burst of flight speed. Move DOUBLE FAR in a mostly straight line, blasting through obstacles with STR and being HARD to hit. 2 SP: Fly with uncanny precision and dynamic trajectory. Describe a wild, fast maneuver such as threading the needle, spinning a turbine, or intercepting a jet. Execute successfully with a STR roll. Minor Powers Nimbus: Generates Light out to FAR against all forms of darkness, including the MOLES darkness power and grants The Green Knight True Sight out to FAR.  The Green Knight can turn the Nimbus on and off. Instant Change from “regular” clothes to armor, shield, weapons and green cape. Fearless: Fear attacks have no effect on The Green Knight Immune to Poison and Disease and no need for oxygen when wearing The Green Knight Armor Effort: Basic (Weapons): 1 Tools: 3 Guns: Energy & Magic: Ultimate: Properties: Impact Resistance Relentless Loot: Stealth Dust: The Green Knight has a pouch that generates magic dust.  Once per day, the Green Knight can use the dust to make a Stealth roll EASY.  This also allows the Green Knight to make a single EASY roll for Stealth for the group of heroes. Equipment: Green Knight Armor: Armor of God Green Knight Shield: Shield of Faith Disadvantages Anachronistic Speech: The Green Knight talks in a manner that tends to offend contemporary listeners.  When speaking, roll a d4.  On a roll of 2, listeners are somewhat offended and will react accordingly and any corresponding persuasion CHA roll by the Green Knight will fail.  On a roll of 1, listeners will become extremely offended and may call law enforcement or record The Green Knight and post the recording on social media or have similar reactions, and any persuasion CHA roll by The Green Knight will fail.  This does not affect player characters.  The player character reactions are up to the players. This weakness also makes it difficult for The Green Knight to interact with voice-activated machines, assuming that he would even attempt such a thing.  Roll a d4, on a 2, the machine does not understand.  On a 1, the machine misunderstands and acts in an unexpected way with potentially disastrous results.This weakness helps with efforts by The Green Knight to provoke anger in listeners.  When using CHA to provoke anger, roll a d20 and add + 2 for CHA as usual and add a d4.  If an EFFORT is also needed in this context, add a d4 to the effort roll.  Use these methods for all CHA rolls if The Green Knight is at a Renaissance Fair. No New Technology: “New” is very broad.  Cannot use modern tools or technology or drive or type and refuses to have a commlink installed in his Armor.  He responds well when Manifester creates an illusion of Military Signal Flags or Musical Horns to correspond to “attack,” “retreat,” “flank,” “fortify,” and similar messages.  The Green Knight’s Tools Effort Bonus only applies to tools that would have existed during or before the 1500s. Background: Alaric was the first born son of a powerful noble. This made his decision to apprentice as a stone mason an unusual one. However, his father believed in hard work and approved of Alaric's decision. From his training he skills that would correspond to masonry as practiced up to and through the 1500s.  He also has skills that would correspond to a much earlier age, like knowing how to butcher an animal.  He may display those sorts of skills in unusual ways, like roasting an animal over an open fire in a public place. He tends to think women with superpowers are witches, but his allies can sometimes talk him out of that. He knew Joan of Arc. He may have been an opponent of hers, but he still respected her, so he does not think all powerful women are diabolical. He thinks modern concepts like separation of church and state and human rights are ridiculous. His conception of “rights” is probably reflected in the Magna Carta, so, for instance, kings are not infallible agents of God, but the notion of democracy is both laughable and terrifying. In modern times Sir Alaric is a legendary knight of the Militis Lucis Divinae, known in myth as The Verdant Warden. sessions/session-27-september-7,-2025.ht.title: Session 27 - September 7, 2025
sessions/session-27-september-7,-2025.ht.description: Session 27, “Little Alcatraz”9/7/2025This is a draft.  Some of the details may be wrong or out of order, such as what information the heroes got from the French Intelligence Officer versus what the heroes learned from Automatic Man.  Also, the sequence of events in the combat is probably wrong and incomplete.  We can update and correct it with notes from the players.A plan starts out badly and ends beautifully.In the 1949 Campaign:The morning after the night at The Carnival, there is a knock at Manifester’s door.  It’s Capone with several of his tough guys.  Capone explains that in the early morning hours a makeshift jail north of the river was attacked by “Jap Supervillains.”  The jail housed “Japs” that were about to get transported to a “camp.”  The jail was partially destroyed and many of the “Japs” escaped.  Capone explains that there’s money to be made in helping Uncle Sam.  Capone says he has equipment and facilities through his connections and is having a river barge converted to a floating jail to hold the “Japs.”  He calls it “Little Alcatraz.”  Capone explains that Government pencil-pushers always have demands.  Capone asks Manifester to lend his “crew” to guarding the jail, so Capone can get approval with the Government, since “Jap super villains” attacked the jail, the pencil-pushers want superheroes signed on with the private jail.  Capone says he’ll pay each of the heroes $50 a day.  Manifester does not like the idea but agrees.  Capone gives him $250.Meanwhile, Captain France goes to the home of Thomas Black (Dissonance) to check on him.  Thomas describes his memory of being attacked by a Japanese man with a “jump pack.”  Thomas remembers falling, but his memory is vague after that until the Heroes rescued him from The Carnival.  Captain France suggests they get food.Back at Manifester’s, after Capone leaves, Automatic Man calls Manifester.  Automatic Man has detected a code in Kansas City Rose’s broadcasts.  He has also been monitoring Government communications.  He has not entirely cracked the Rose Code, but he has determined that there was a lot of chatter associated with the attack on the makeshift jail.  Automatic Man used Ye Olde Floppy Disk and determined that the amount of chatter is beyond what would be expected based on the nature of the attack mission.  There must be something more going on.Manifester contacts Captain France by walkie-talkie.  Manifester, Captain France, and Dissonance meet at Town Topic Hamburgers.  Manifester tells them about the job from Capone and the call from Automatic Man.  Manifester gives each of them $40.  They get food.  Captain France says the heroes must save the Japanese-Americans.  The three heroes talk about what to do.  A man sitting at the diner bar says something about locking all the Japs up.  Captain France disagrees with him.  The man yells, “Remember the USS Arizona!”  Captain France punches him, knocking him out.  The diners flee.  Soon there are police sirens in the distance.  The three heroes leave the restaurant after leaving a big tip.Captain France gets a special signal on his walkie-talkie that tells him to call his French Intelligence Officer.  He calls a special number from a hotel pay phone.  After some confusion over the correct response to “Johnny has a long mustache,” Captain France learns that Japanese Supervillains attacked the jail.  That call combined with another discussion with Automatic Man gets the heroes information about three Japanese Anomalies: Ozeki, Nihon, and Emperor’s Blade.  Automatic Man tells them that several of the Japanese-Americans who were “liberated” from the makeshift jail were later found decapitated.  Automatic Man also tells them that the Japanese Anomalies were looking for the Emperor’s Grandson among the Japanese prisoners.  The Japanese call him “Nico,” which means “cat.”  The Japanese Anomalies intend to kill him as a traitor. The Heroes get a ride from Sebastian, the driver provided to them by Capone, to the river to view Little Alcatraz.  The Barge is in the Missouri River in an industrial area a few hundred west (upstream) from a railroad bridge and a street bridge.  There are about a dozen of Capone’s henchmen on the bank with machine guns.  There is walkway out to the barge.  Workers are building a canopy on the barge.  Other workers are placing red barrels on the barge.  Manifester recalls something Capone said and realizes the red barrels are gasoline.  There are a dozen men of Japanese descent chained together and chained to the barge.  Two bots are working on the barge.  A tugboat is keeping the barge in place. The Heroes discuss a plan and go get Italian food.  The heroes plan more and come back after dark.  Manifester teleports onto the rail bridge east of Little Alcatraz.  The barge is now anchored in the middle of the river with the tugboat hooked to the barge.  There are two groups of Capone Henchmen with machine guns on the bank on each side of the river.  The Heroes plan to have Manifester create a portal and then move the barge toward the portal and teleport the prisoners through the portal. Captain France tells the Capone Henchman that he is going on the barge to guard it.  He uses his jetpack to fly Rocketeer-style onto the barge.Dissonance flies onto the barge.  Captain France goes into the cabin of the tugboat. Manifester creates an illusion of large ship headed toward the tugboat and barge from the west.  Dissonance creates a loud noise to go with the illusion. The robot in the tugboat begins moving the tugboat and barge downstream toward the rail bridge. Manifester hears the metal of the rail bridge whine as someone who is very heavy leaps from the rail bridge onto the barge.  It is Ozeki, the Japanese sumo.  The barge pitches when Ozeki lands on it.  Dissonance is thrown into the river.Manifester creates the portal downstream from the barge.Captain France moves from the tugboat to the barge and politely greets Ozeki.  Ozeki tells Captain France to prepare to die.Dissonance flies up from the water and blasts Ozeki with sonic energy, causing his giant body to undulate and quiver.Ozeki rips the chain out of the barge and pitches it into the river with enough force that three of the prisoners and pulled into the river and others are starting to slide toward the edge of the barge. A woman begins flying in from the west toward the barge.  She is wearing white and red robes and is surrounded by bright light.  It is Nihon. Capone’s Henchmen on the north bank of the river begin firing their machine guns at the barge.  They hit only Ozeki.  His huge body ripples again, absorbing much of the damage with only minimal harm to him. Manifester tries to create an illusion of other people for Capone’s Henchmen to fire at and fails. Ozeki charges at Captain France sumo-style.  Captain France successfully holds his ground near the edge of the barge.Dissonance flies over and lifts the chain that is in the river, getting the men in the river above water and close enough to the barge to grab it. The north side of the river explodes with an energy blast from Nihon.  Two Cadillacs explode into the air and collapse again burning on the bank.  Several of the henchmen are killed.  The others on the north bank flee.Manifester creates an illusion impairing Nihon’s vision.Captain France has a sumo-style contest of strength against Ozeki and succeeds in throwing Ozeki into the river.   Nihon blasts a beam of light into the river, creating a massive steam explosion, which almost freaks out Captain France, but he composes himself.On the barge, a space in the air shimmers and opens.  A man in a samurai outfit steps onto the barge.  It is Emperor’s Blade.  He drives a knife into a link of chain pinning it in place and draws his sword and stands over one of the prisoners.  He says something angry in Japanese and raises his sword prepared to decapitate him.Captain France tries to throw a barrel of gas (that he’s been holding since he politely greeted Ozeki) at Emperor’s Blade.  He misses.  Manifester tries to create an illusion of bees stinging Emperor’s Blade.  He fails.  Dissonance flies over and phases through the prisoner, placing himself in the way of Emperor’s Blade.  Emperor’s Blade slashes Dissonance.  Dissonance is seriously wounded.   The tugboat begins to sink as Ozeki grabs it to try to get out of the river.Manifester tries again to create an illusion of bees stinging Emperor’s Blade and succeeds, doing significant damage to Emperor’s Blade. Emperor’s Blade yells something in Japanese.  The air near Emperor’s Blade shimmers again and he disappears.  Nihon begins to glow brighter.  The heroes realize this is bad.Dissonance blast Nihon with sonic energy, but Nihon still glows brighter.Captain France runs, grabs the chain that is attached to the prisoner, and leaps through the portal, pulling the prisoners with him and transporting himself and them onto the railway bridge.  Dissonance flies through the portal, transporting himself to the railway bridge.  At the last instance, Manifester creates an illusion of the prisoners still stuck on the barge as the barge explodes from Nihon’s energy blast attack.  The massive explosion lights up the night sky from the combined power of the energy attack and the exploding barrels of gasoline.On the railway bridge, Captain France pulls up the chain to lift prisoners who are hanging from it.  Dissonance silences the sound of the chain and the prisoners until all the prisoners are safely on the railway bridge.

sessions/session-2.html.title: Session 2
sessions/session-2.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 10–11, 2022 Dimension: 24 April 10 (Sunday): Mark Renallo approaches Mantis Shrimp with two enforcers. After an autograph exchange, they go to brunch, during which Mark reveals his distrust of federal agents and explains his involvement in various illicit enterprises, including parties, drugs, and prostitution.
Mark reveals that The Gnome, a weaponsmith, had planned to sell a new weapon to Golden Dome, but the deal now has a different buyer. Mark fears the weapon will cause chaos and urges the heroes to intervene in the upcoming exchange at 9th and Wyandotte. April 11 (Monday): The session opens mid-scene (“Segment 3”) during the weapons exchange.
Templar ambushes two “agents” observing the parking garage and rappels from the third story to ground level.
Mantis Shrimp shrinks just as a man with a case (likely the weapon) stands beside another with a duffle bag.
A BMW accelerates toward the pair; gunfire erupts as a shot pierces the car’s windshield from behind Mantis Shrimp.
Manifester (Larry Harry Jones) observes from nearby, already in costume. A black cloud of darkness rises from the ground behind the transaction, signaling the arrival of an unknown hostile force.
Mantis Shrimp – Investigating the street-level exchange, disguised as a street performer playing accordion.
Templar – Attacks surveillance agents and joins the fray by rappelling down the garage.
Larry Harry Jones – Watching the transaction unfold in hero form, ready to intervene.
The Gnome – Weaponsmith whose advanced rifle or device is the object of the exchange. Unknown “agents” – Possibly federal or private operatives watching the scene. Black Cloud Entity – Emerges during the transaction; its nature and purpose remain unclear.
Mark Renallo – Shady entrepreneur with ties to organized crime, uneasy ally to the heroes. Unnamed buyers and sellers at the exchange, one holding a case (likely the weapon) and another a duffle bag. Driver of the BMW, involved in the violent exchange. This session transitions the story from public spectacle to street-level intrigue.
The introduction of Mark Renallo and The Gnome expands the Kansas City underworld and hints at a dangerous weapons market involving super-tech. The closing scene establishes the arrival of an unknown dark force, setting up escalating supernatural or anomalous threats.Session 2 – (Played 11/16/22) In game: Sunday April 10
Mark Renallo drives up alongside Mantis Shrimp with two beefy guys. Gets out. Gets autograph. Goes to brunch with Mantis. Mark hates feds. Runs seedy businesses – parties, drugs, prostitutes. Knows that The Gnome (a weapon smith) was going to sell a special weapon to Golden Dome, but now has a new buyer. Mark doesn’t want the weapon on the street. 9th and Wyandotte tomorrow – exchange weapon made by The Gnome. Think it’s some form of rifle. Monday April 11 Just finished segment 3.
Templar just hit two “agents” who were pretending to look at a car while watching parking lot in parking garage around 3rd story from top. Templar then rappelled down parking garage (turn in Segment 5) down to the ground.
Mantis Shrimp has just gone small (END 46) right in front of guy holding case (assumed to contain the weapon) who is next to guy holding duffle bag. Guy in BMW just hit the gas, gunning it towards Mantis/Duffle/Case guys. Gunshot came from behind Mantis into BMW windshield. (Mantis is holding an accordion—he was busking (badly) as a cover for hanging out on the street).
Larry Harry Jones is crouched within view of the transaction and Mantis, changed into his hero outfit. Black cloud of darkness has just emerged from ground behind the transaction.

sessions/session-3.html.title: Session 3
sessions/session-3.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 11, 2022 Dimension: 24 Weapons Exchange Turns Violent: Continuing from the prior session’s standoff, chaos erupts at the parking garage near 9th and Wyandotte. Mantis Shrimp resizes just as a BMW speeds toward the weapons dealers, launching the car over their heads and causing it to crash. The Arrival of Trenchcoat: A mysterious figure in a trench coat exits the Handsy Plumber van and attacks with energy blasts, disabling several Khaki Techs (federal-style agents). Just get the bag.” [Paul says:] Only Mantis Shrimp perceives the voice directly and sees color distortions invisible to normal humans. Retreat into the Tunnel: The M.O.L.E.S. retrieve the duffle bag and withdraw underground. Mantis Shrimp pursues them into the darkness while Templar regroups in the parking garage.
Manifester confronts Trenchcoat, stunning him with a psychic assault before the mysterious figure loads an injured man into the van. Scene Ends: Combat pauses with heroes divided—Mantis in the tunnel, Templar ascending the parking garage, and Manifester standing near Trenchcoat and the van.

Larry Harry Jones – Uses teleportation, psychic powers, and illusions to protect civilians and disorient enemies. M.O.L.E.S. – Blobby, semi-corporeal dark entities operating from an underground tunnel network. Ashen-Skinned Figure – Possibly the leader or controller of the M.O.L.E.S.; displays energy-based and psychic powers. sessions/session-4.html.title: Session 4
sessions/session-4.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 11, 2022 Dimension: 24 Van and Tunnel Chaos: The fight resumes as Trenchcoat (later revealed to be Automatic Man 2.0) jumps into the back of a self-driving van that begins to back away from the tunnel. Mantis Shrimp continues battling within the darkness of the tunnel, glimpsing the shadowy slope ahead and hearing the disembodied voice again: “Simple creature, don’t engage with him. He’s insane.” Barbara Appears:
A tall, athletic woman with pale skin and long dark hair—identified as Barbara—emerges from the tunnel, holding high heels and wearing a fur wrap. The telepathic voice chastises her for trying to leave, saying: “Barbara, what are you doing? … I knew I should have scanned your mind.”
Manifester teleports between Barbara and the dark blob, posing dramatically. The voice calls him “the amateur.” Manifester’s indignant response: “Who are you calling an amateur!?” Escalation in the Garage:
Templar races upward through the parking structure, encountering recovering agents and heading for the roof. Mantis Shrimp battles another MOLE in the tunnel while more blobs emerge. Barbara Flees and The Master Speaks: Barbara runs from the tunnel, shouting, “I’m getting away from you lunatic!” The M.O.L.E.S. pursue her as Manifester and Mantis coordinate: Manifester will protect Barbara while Mantis holds off the pursuers. Automatic Man’s Awakening: The darkness enveloping Trenchcoat disrupts an implanted control device on his arm, freeing him from external manipulation. He realizes: He has been deactivated for 8 days and reactivated 6 days ago. A Bluetooth-like transmitter at the municipal airport has been controlling him. He possesses two holographic memory spheres, one sealed, one new. The van is packed with explosives, rigged to detonate if it moves too far from a particular case.
He disables the control system and regains his identity as Automatic Man 2.0. Battle Expands:
Templar reaches the roof, breaking through a door; Mantis Shrimp throws vehicles in combat with the M.O.L.E.S. but misses spectacularly, launching a VW Bug over Manifester. Automatic Man disables his captor’s tech, subdues a Khaki Tac, and bends his shotgun into a bowtie. Barbara’s Rescue and Revelation:
Manifester teleports Barbara to safety. She reveals that the voice belongs to The Master, a telepath who imprisoned her in “the Underworld.” Manifester vows to protect her. Arrival of New Threats:
The Master emerges from the tunnel, floating and surveying the battle. Nearby, Templar records video as a fiery streak approaches—Fire Cube. Climactic Moments:
Mantis Shrimp unknowingly carries the case containing the bomb away from the van, increasing the detonation risk.
Automatic Man 2.0 tells Mantis he’s trying to stop the explosion; Mantis agrees to distract the M.O.L.E.S.
Fire Cube arrives dramatically—“I am Fire Cube! You shall feel my fury!”—but is immediately blasted backward by Automatic Man. Templar fires on Automatic Man, missing narrowly with a blinding beam.
Fire Cube retaliates, shouting, “You’ll feel the heat of my fury!” Manifester teleports closer to rejoin the fray as the scene closes.
Mantis Shrimp – Continues the physical fight with the M.O.L.E.S., accidentally carries the bomb away from its proximity field.
Templar – Navigates the garage and fires on Automatic Man, unaware he’s now an ally.
Larry Harry Jones – Protects Barbara, uses illusions and teleportation, and engages in a battle of wills with The Master.
Automatic Man 2.0 – Regains control of his mind and body, disables his captor’s device, and reenters the fight with renewed purpose.
The Master – Revealed as the telepathic voice manipulating Barbara and likely responsible for controlling Automatic Man.
M.O.L.E.S. – Reappear as the dark entities emerging from the tunnel, pursuing Barbara.
Fire Cube – Fiery, egotistical new arrival; declares vengeance but is swiftly repelled.
Barbara – Former captive of The Master, attempts escape; reveals her psychic imprisonment in the “Underworld.” Khaki Tacs – Federal-type agents still active in the area. Audi Driver – Civilian caught in the chaos; his car becomes part of the illusion used against The Master. Session 4 marks the dramatic unmasking of Trenchcoat as Automatic Man and the first direct reference to The Master as an active antagonist. Barbara’s escape provides a human link to the Underworld storyline, while Fire Cube’s arrival expands the roster of powered figures in Kansas City. The heroes remain divided, the bomb unresolved, and the threat of The Master looming.Session 4 (1/15/22) In game: Monday April 11 continued Trenchcoat jumps in back of van which begins backing away; beeping. Nobody is driving. In the dark, Mantis hits. A darkness blob hits back to front of hole giving Mantis some view. Sees sloping down tunnel with a dark blob in front of him. The eerie voice says “Simple creature don’t engage with him. He’s insane.” Templar makes it to second floor of garage. Peaks down, sees a dark blob pop out of the tunnel; van moving slowly backwards. Templar takes a shot at tires of van… van is obviously very heavily armored. Mantis tries to tackle blob deeper in tunnel but whiffs. Hears something go past him. Others see tall athletic woman, pale skin, long dark hair, wearing fur and carrying high heels emerge from hole. The voice says “Barbara what are you doing? I thought we were learning to trust each other. You said if I allowed you to observe today, you wouldn’t try to leave. I knew I should have scanned your mind.” Manifester teleports between woman and blob with big flourish and strikes a threatening pose facing the blob. Voice “don’t bother with him the amateur, just get Barbara.” Manifest shouts “Who are you calling an amateur!?” Templar runs up to fourth floor, sees agents on floor 3 are up and opened trunk of their car on his way. Mantis swings out again and misses. A second something moves past Mantis. Others see another blob come out of the tunnel. A blob tries to run around Manifester. Van makes it out to the street. Manifester kicks out at the darkness but misses. Templar grabs duffle and heads for roof. Mantis runs to the front of the tunnel. Van is in street. A gray Audi honks at van. Trenchcoat gets out of van, grabs khaki tac. Barbara continues running away, yelling “I’m getting away from you lunatic!” Templar still running. Mantis runs out of the hole, talks to Manifester who says “they’re chasing that woman. You slow them down and I’ll help her.” Mantis tries slide tackle at a blob… slides into the darkness and out the other side. Manifester teleports toward Barbara. Moles move try to corral Barbara; darkness of one engulfs Trenchcoat. AUTOMATIC MAN (BRETT WAS TRENCHCOAT ALL ALONG) feels some kind of system anomaly somewhat like pain. He sees a device attached to his upper left arm, feels a Bluetooth-like signal has been coming from it. Can tell internal security system ability has been disabled for six days. He realizes it’s only because he’s engulfed in darkness that is blocking all electromagnetic waves that the Bluetooth device is stopped. He disables device properly. He knows he has been deactivated 14 days ago (for 8 days). Realizes he was “stolen” or “kidnapped” from his lab. Has partial memory of what’s going on. Someone has been sending him on missions for six days. He has two holographic memory spheres that he cannot access. Always had one that was sealed but surprised because now there are two. Realizes van is filled with explosives and has proximity trigger that will explode if gets too far from a case. Templar gets to a door to the roof. Kicks it. Smashes through the deadbolt and it flies open. Mantis goes spinning windmill style into the nearest dark blob, swinging arms and tail, manages to backhand a mole moving it about ten feet, crashing into a vehicle. Audi guy continues to beep. Templar looks out, sees no obvious targets. Mantis tries chucking a VW Bug at the other MOLE, but overshoots, flies over Manifester and car smashes into parked cars. Automatic Man attempts to disable the proximity detector inside the van but cannot locate it. He begins walking, still having khaki tac slung over his shoulder. Guy in Audi screams, tries to back up, hits a parked truck and leaves his car. AM puts down khaki tac on sidewalk. Bends his shotgun into a bowtie. Manifester takes Barbara by the arm, says “Trust me, but this will be disconcerting” and teleports as far down street as he can then asks “Who was that voice?” B: That is The Master. He is a terrible person and a telepath. He’s been holding me in the Underworld. Manif: I am going to get you to safety, Barbara. Not to be overly familiar but I heard your voice in my head. Templar sees someone in dark clothing with bulbous head float out of the hole and hover into the air, looking around. Mantis observes the glowing light and notes AM on the sidewalk. AM can tell device that was controlling him has signal coming from municipal airport. AM asks Mantis what is going on, who are they fighting. Mantis says him and also the MOLES. Fire Cube starts flying towards Templar saying “You’ll feel the heat of my fury!” Mantis continues running shrunken with the bomb under cars, unfortunately away from the van with proximity monitor. Manif: Do you know who the cube guy is? B: I don’t know him. He’s not with the Master. Manif: Stay here. He teleports towards the action but a safe distance from Automatic Man. sessions/session-6.html.title: Session 6
sessions/session-6.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 11, 2022 Dimension: 24 Interrogation and Tension: The heroes regroup in the Bossanova Hotel penthouse. Mantis Shrimp examines the captured MOLE, finding thick, loose skin and fur, and no tech devices. Manifester questions Barbara about The Master’s plans—she explains that he preaches survival through usefulness and wealth, believing humans will eventually destroy anomalies. The Knock at the Door:
Templar spots a bald, suited man (Telly Savalas look-alike) through the door peephole. Automatic Man 2.0 hides The Master and the MOLE in the bathroom before opening it. The visitor—Maxwell Manning, Automatic Man’s old bandmate—bursts in enthusiastically, announcing a gig that night at The Majestic: setup at 8 PM, play at 9. Automatic Man plays keytar in Maxwell Manning and the First Laws, a jazz-rock fusion band in the Herbie Hancock style. Mantis and Renallo:
Mantis Shrimp escorts the unconscious MOLE to police headquarters. En route, he encounters Mark Renallo arguing with the hotel clerk. Renallo drives Mantis downtown and shares that he doubts the explosion was The Gnome’s weapon—it was supposed to be reusable. He believes the real weapon is a robot. Mantis drops the MOLE off at the precinct, labels it an unregistered anomaly, and departs before questions start. Interrogating The Master:
Back at the hotel, Templar has The Master at gunpoint while Barbara urges his execution.

sessions/session-6.5.html.title: Session 6.5 – Special Interlude #1
sessions/session-6.5.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 11, 2022 Dimension: 24 Mission from The Order: Templar receives a directive from The Order to investigate a reported anomaly battle at St. Mary’s Episcopal Church. The rumor: a terrifying “beast” that seems unkillable. He is joined by Larry Harry Jones and Mantis Shrimp. The Journey: The trio travels in Manifester’s beat-up 1995 Celica, with “Hysteria” playing endlessly on a loop. During the drive, Leandra calls Manifester wondering why he isn’t at John’s Big Deck; he assures her he’s on his way. Pursuit and Arrival: The heroes notice a suspicious, government-looking van tailing them. Manifester maneuvers skillfully to lose it, and they continue to St. Mary’s. With no parking available, they park illegally—Manifester cleverly places an old ticket on the windshield and chalks the tire. “It’s all about illusion, gentlemen.” At the Church Scene: Police tape marks the area around a reflection garden. A chain-link fence has been cut. Several officers and a white unmarked car (with police plates) are present. Mantis Shrimp approaches the police, casually engaging them (one asks for a selfie). He notices blood across multiple spots. Templar, unseen, inspects the police car. Inside, he spots a brown evidence bag with tape but can’t unlock the door. When an officer begins to notice Templar, Mantis distracts him further. Mantis collects a blood sample on his finger while pretending to help. Police tell Mantis the evidence tech (with the car keys) is inside the church. Illusions and Distraction: From across the street, Manifester texts Leandra about “car trouble,” while creating an illusion of a distressed dog trapped in a nearby vehicle. A nearby officer, completely fooled, rushes off to investigate. Local Connections: Officer Tom (married to Becky), a contact of Mantis, introduces the team to Genevieve and Ezekiel—details unspecified but likely linked to the church or scene. Wrap-up: The trio leaves quietly after gathering evidence. Manifester drops Templar at a Catholic church, then takes Mantis home before heading to meet Leandra at John’s Big Deck.
Templar – Sent by The Order to investigate; collects a blood sample from the scene.
Larry Harry Jones – Handles misdirection with illusions and police distractions, covers the group’s approach.
Mantis Shrimp – Engages officers, distracts them, and secures a blood sample. Tom (Officer) – Police contact of Mantis; introduces Genevieve and Ezekiel. Genevieve and Ezekiel – Connected to the church; limited interaction. Leandra – Contacts Manifester during the mission, unaware of the situation. This interlude bridges the major plotline with a side investigation. The encounter at St. Mary’s hints at a potentially ongoing anomaly threat—“the unkillable beast”—and deepens the city’s atmosphere of tension between authorities and anomalies. Light humor contrasts with the grim setting, offering a breather before the main story resumes.Special Interlude Number 1 (3/4/23) Still Monday, April 11 Templar, Manifester, and Mantis head to St. Mary’s Episcopal Church to investigate an anomaly battle; an alarming “beast” who seems unkillable. The Order sent Templar. As we leave in the 1995 beat up Celica, Hysteria constantly plays on a loop. Lovely Leandra calls Manifester asking why he’s not at Johns Big Deck. He says he’s on his way. Realize they’re being followed by a van, looks like a government type. Manifester tries to lose them. They stop pursuing after a while. Manifester drives to the church. They can’t find parking, so just park illegally. Manifester puts an old ticket on the window and skillfully marks his tire with chalk. “It’s all about illusion, gentlemen.” Outside church is some police tape. Chain link fence around a reflection area is cut. There are police milling about. There is a lab-type vehicle; white unmarked car with cop plates. Mantis walks up to the scene, greets police officers there. One asks for a selfie. As Mantis distracts police, Templar goes to the car undetected. See brown bag in back seat with evidence tape on it. Door of car is locked. Templar attempts to jimmy the lock but failed. An officer starts to look over Mantis towards the car, but Mantis notices and distracts him. Mantis sees blood in many locations. Talking to the police he scoops up blood onto his finger. He asks for evidence bagging equipment they say it’s in the car. On other side of street, Manifester is texting Leandra about car problems. Mantis heads toward the car saying “oh hey! It’s my buddy Templar.” The cops say they don’t have key to the evidence car, the lab tech does and she’s in the church. But Templar pulls out a swab and takes the sample from Mantis’ finger. There are 4 police with Mantis. Manifester picks on cop and makes illusion of a dog in great distress inside a car down the street. Officer is completely convinced. He heads over to the truck. Tom (wife Becky) – cop Mantis knows. Introduces them to Genevieve and Ezekiel. They leave. Manifester drops off Templar at the Catholic Church and takes Mantis home before circling around to meet Leandra at John’s Big Deck.

sessions/session-7.html.title: Session 7
sessions/session-7.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 11, 2022 Dimension: 24 Lies and Logistics: Larry Harry Jones spins an elaborate story to Leandra, claiming his Celica was towed as abandoned while he was at QuikTrip buying a taquito, preventing him from meeting her at John’s Big Deck. The Investigation Begins:
The team—Templar, Mantis Shrimp, Automatic Man 2.0, and Manifester—regroups at the Bossanova Hotel and drives to Briarcliff to investigate The Gnome’s location and the rumored geodesic dome facility nearby. Suspicious Containers: They find shipping containers near The Gnome’s supposed apartment. Templar scopes the area, spotting only boxes and ordinary items, but notices a powered refrigeration unit labeled in Korean: “Wuhon Institute of Virology.” Mantis Shrimp pries open a container, discovering neatly arranged cases, a small fridge with vials of glowing green fluid (smelling of acidic lime). He pockets one vial. The group finds no documents but several energy weapons. Mantis keeps one small weapon, giving two others (large and small) to Templar. Police Arrival:
Automatic Man 2.0 intercepts a 911 call reporting the disturbance, even identifying the caller’s number. Mantis, feigning civic duty, calls 911 himself to “report a suspicious shipping container.” He sits casually atop the opened container, chatting on the phone as two police cars screech in. Officer Michaels recognizes him: “Mantis Shrimp!” After inspecting the scene, they cuff and arrest him. Mantis slips free of one cuff, calls anomaly lawyer Paul Hood, and theatrically declares, “On advice of my lawyer, I must bail.” He rips open the car door and escapes, arranging to meet the team at Mimi’s Pantry. Unknown Caller: When they regroup, Automatic Man’s satellite phone rings. A cryptic voice says: “Did you get the paper? Did you get The Star? … The Spring Training will be illuminating, don’t you think?” The line goes dead. Men in Black Surveillance:
Templar senses unease—too many open sightlines near the dome. Through his scope, he spots two observers in a black car: an Asian man and an older “Abe Vigoda–looking” companion.
Manifester creates an illusion making the older man believe he’s being swarmed by ants, causing him real distress and distracting his partner. The group dashes to the dome. Inside the Geodesic Dome:
As they approach, Templar’s x-ray vision fails to penetrate the structure, and Manifester notes its alien-like texture—reminiscent of Roswell rumors.
A camera above the entrance tracks Automatic Man 2.0. When he steps forward, the door opens automatically. Inside, the space resembles a lush greenhouse, filled with fruit-bearing plants tended by boxy robots. The door seals behind them, cutting off cell service. A voice from a speaker greets them: “Did you see the second Royals game last Tuesday? That game was a lot of fun.” AM checks the box score—there was indeed a mysterious second game recorded as 10–10. When he speaks the score aloud, the room rotates, and a floor drain opens to reveal a spiral staircase descending below. Descent into the Facility: They descend into a square chamber (12x12 ft) lined with downward-facing spigots. A robot on tracks greets them: “Four visitors.” A bulkhead door slides aside, revealing another chamber and a robot labeled “Twelve.” It recognizes “Mr. Von Neuman” (Automatic Man) and welcomes him. A second bulkhead opens into a vast hallway filled with robots, monitors, and advanced machinery. One screen plays Buck Rogers, another an old India vs. West Indies cricket match. Dr. Goodfellow: A humanoid robot introduces himself as Dr. Goodfellow, greeting Automatic Man warmly: “When the Gnome and the Fiddler had their battle, I fooled their sensors into thinking this facility was destroyed.” Manifester quips, “Technically that was an illusion. A trick is what a whore does for money.” Dr. G explains that his memories of their disagreement were deleted, but he recalls it involved a dispute of method—the Gnome sought action, the Fiddler preferred observation. The Inverted Mayan Long Calendar: Dr. Goodfellow now works on the “Inverted Mayan Long Calendar,” an analytical model predicting future crises. He invites the team to “hear a bit of the future,” combining random inputs into a bizarre prophecy: “In the next 3–5 days, a very significant event involving 317.576 trustworthy, stationary trout.”
Automatic Man 2.0 senses the entire structure is akin to a land-based submarine. Revelations About the Past:
Automatic Man 2.0 learns he was built by The Fiddler.
Dr. Goodfellow explains: The Fiddler is a human male, 6'1.25", 184 lbs, committed to human survival.
The Gnome and the Fiddler’s rivalry endangered CRICKET’s goals.
Automatic Man 2.0 was created as an envoy—the intermediary between humans and future AI. The bots have grown eccentric, fixating on cricket and Buck Rogers.
When Mantis Shrimp asks how Fiddler would view him, Dr. G replies coldly: “Fiddler would not see you as human.”
Automatic Man 2.0 – Traces more of his origin; recognized as “Mr. Von Neuman” by the dome’s AI network.
Templar – Provides overwatch, spots surveillance, and observes alien technology.
Mantis Shrimp – Breaks into containers, steals samples and energy weapons, arrested and escapes dramatically.
Larry Harry Jones – Employs illusions and wit to distract enemies and assist infiltration; provides comic counterpoint.
Leandra – Briefly contacted by Manifester; unaware of the larger mission.
Mark Renallo – Not present but still tied to the Gnome plotline.
Dr. Goodfellow – Robotic scientist, caretaker of the dome and researcher of predictive futures.
The Fiddler – Revealed as Automatic Man’s creator and former CRICKET leader.
The Gnome – Mentioned as Fiddler’s counterpart in the CRICKET schism. Officer Michaels – Arrests Mantis before his comedic escape. Abe Vigoda-type agent & partner – Men in Black surveillance team. This session reveals Automatic Man’s true creator (The Fiddler) and the nature of the CRICKET conflict. Dr. Goodfellow’s introduction expands the mythos of anomaly-linked AI and predictive systems. Humor, tension, and philosophy collide—blending noir absurdity with revelations about free will, machine evolution, and human survival. Session 7 (4/14/23) Everyone meets up at the hotel again. Manifester tells Leandra an elaborate lie about the Celica being towed as abandoned while he was at a Quick Trip getting a taquita and having to go get it from the impound lot so he can’t meet her at John’s Big Deck. The gang decides to head up to Briarcliff area to investigate the geodesic dome and the Gnome. They pull up outside where the Gnome is expected to be. Templar and Mantis are able to see the Gnome’s apartment. There are suspicious shipping containers outside. Templar sees just boxes and packed away items inside, nothing obviously suspicious. Only odd thing is that there’s a power source inside and seems to be refrigerated items. Writing on outside is Korean, says “Wuhon Institute of Virology.” AM monitors cell phones but hears nothing obvious. Templar looks for security systems. Sees only a lock. Mantis rips open one of the doors. Inside are nicely organized cases and materials including a small refrigerator. Mantis opens the fridge. Small cases with vials of greenish fluid inside. Mantis sniffs one. Smells like very acidic lime. Mantis pockets one vial. No documents in the container. AM hears cell phone call to the police. He is able to get the phone number calling 911. Mantis opens a box and finds unusual looking weapons inside. They appear to be energy weapons. Mantis keeps a tiny one, and gives one big and one small one to Templar. Mantis calls 911 too. Tells them that they should send someone down to check out weird shipping container. They say they have officers on the way. Others disperse to watch. Mantis leaves on his cell phone so they can hear him; sits on top of the shipping container at the open door swinging his legs. Two squad cars come screaming into the parking lot, pull up to Mantis. Officers step out, guns drawn. One yells “Mantis Shrimp!” They pat Mantis down. They inspect the container, asking Mantis about how it got opened. Officer says “we have to check this out. We know where to meet you.” Officer Michaels. Mantis comes clean about ripping open the door. Officer Michael says we’ll need to arrest Mantis. He gets placed in handcuffs and placed in police car. The others call an Uber and get out of there. Mantis slips out of a handcuff and calls his lawyer, famed anomaly defense attorney Paul Hood. He asks if he can “bail out,” so Mantis tells Officer Michael, “on advise of my lawyer, I must bail,” rips open the door, jumps out of the squad car. Walking away as the squad car screeches and turns around he calls Automatic Man. “I bailed out! I’ll meet you at the Mimi’s Pantry?” and he starts walking. The Uber riders arrive first. Mantis walks and arrives a bit later. AM’s satellite phone rings. “Did you get the paper? Did you get the Star?” “Yeah!” “The Spring Training will be illuminating [??], don’t you think?” they hand up. He doesn’t know who they were. Templar has the heebie-jeebies bc there are lots of open lines of sight everywhere, seems unsafe. Lots of unobstructed views down to the geodesic dome. Templar takes scope and investigates the surroundings. Spots Asian man in men-in-black car with Abe Pagoda-looking guy. Templar tells everyone the men-in-black guys are staking out the surroundings from near the garage. Manifester admits can only affect one target at a time. But he targets Abe Pagoda-looking guy to think he stepped in an ant hill and entire body is being swarmed by ants, intending to also distract his partner. Illusion is so powerful, he is even injured some by the ants. We hear an older man screaming (Abe) and Asian guy is very distracted. The squad runs to the dome. Templar notes his x-ray vision will not penetrate the dome as they approach. Manifester feels material looks like stuff people say was recovered from Roswell; seems alien-like. Security camera above the door, but door opens as AM approaches. On the inside it looks like a greenhouse. We step inside. Rows and rows of fruit bearing plants on raised beds, we cannot recognize them. Box-shaped robot is tending to the plants and ignores us. Door closes behind us and closes behind us with a sealing noise. Templar notices there is no cell phone service. Security camera focuses on AM. “Friend of yours?” Manifester asks. Speakerbox below the camera says “did you see the second Royals game last Tuesday” (same voice as called him earlier). “that game was a lot of fun.” AM checks the box score. He doesn’t remember there being a second game that night but the paper does note a second game with score 10-10. When we say the score, the room begins to slowly spin. A drain in the floor opens to reveal a spiral staircase. We head down the stairs. Leads down 20ft to a lighted chamber. Drain door closes as we go down. Chamber is 12’x12’ square. Each wall has downward facing spigot-like things on wall. There is a bulky robot on wheels on a track. When we arrive, it says “Four visitors.” A bulkhead door moves out and slides left. There is a similar robot in neck chamber: “Please step in and do not block the door.” It asks for our names. It gives its name as “twelve.” 12 knows Mr. Von Neuman. Second bulkhead door opens. Beyond that one is long hallway ~80ft long, 20ft wide. Shelves on walls, tables and stands in middle, various robots moving about. TV on wall shows Buck Rogers episodes. Another TV shows India vs West Indes cricket game seemingly from the 1980s. Floor is on two levels, walkway with center floor below. Very advanced robot or replicant approaches us smiling, greets AM and introduces himself as Dr. Goodfellow. AM does not remember him but Dr. G is very happy to have him here. “You know, when the Gnome and the Fiddler had their battle, I pulled a trick on them so their sensors thought this facility was destroyed.” Manifester: “technically that was an illusion. A trick is what a whore does for money.” Dr. G Confides reason for disagreement was deleted from his memory but thinks it was about method. Gnome wanted action; Fiddler wanted observation. Now he can work on the Inverted Mayan Long Calendar his passion project rather than setting the predictions of Nostradamus to quatrains. “would you like to hear a bit of the future?” YES! Has one of us pick a number, adjective, adjective/adverb, and one picks a noun. Dr G explains more about the Mayan Long Calendar. “In the next 3-5 days a very significant event involving 317.576 trustworthy, stationary trout.” AM gets impression this is the equivalent of a land-based submarine. Templar tells Dr. G about the men in black watching them. Robots make noises as West Indies scores in the cricket match. AM – I’ve been here before correct? Yes Mantis – what are you doing? Research! The bots have gotten quirky. They have become fascinated in cricket and Buck Rogers. AM – where do you know me from? From my involvement with the gnome, fiddler and cricket. You are part of the reason I’m trying to predict the future to determine when and how threatening the rise of AI will be. You’re the envoy. The intermediary between homo sapiens and eventual AI technology. AM – who built me? The fiddler. Mantis – What is Fiddler like? Human 6’1.25” weights 184 lbs. white male. Little interest in sports. Committed to long term survival of human species and civilization. I was developed to help determine the most significant threats to civilization. I can exercise independent judgment which led me to conclude the conflict between gnome and fiddler would doom our efforts. Fiddler would not see Mantis as human.

sessions/session-8.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 11, 2022 Dimension: 1 Exit from the Dome: The team departs the geodesic dome after Dr. Goodfellow shouts “Eureka!” from within. In their vehicle, they find a locked metal suitcase keyed to Mantis Shrimp’s thumbprint, containing: $250 cash ID for “Claude” Miniature firearm Hazmat suit Backpack device Karate gi with black belt Strange Shifts in Reality:
When Manifester starts the car, the usual “Hysteria” track is replaced by “All I Need Is a Miracle.” The car also appears cleaner, with upgraded fast-food wrappers. They spot unusual changes across Kansas City: Roadside celebrity cutouts featuring Mantis Shrimp A new light rail system Barry’s trailer looks different Radio references President Harris, not Biden The Trout Blimp: A fish-shaped blimp marked Freddy the Fisherman’s Trout House advertises a phone number: 816-317-576*. Calling reveals the blimp was stolen. Mantis vows to retrieve it. Chaos on the Bridge: The team heads toward the Buck O’Neil Bridge, where the giant trout blimp is wedged into the bridge entrance, halting traffic. Someone has written “I am a bomb” on its side.
Templar senses movement atop the bridge. REO Speedwagon’s “Time for Me to Fly” begins playing, compelling people to dance uncontrollably. Arrival of Meat Shield: A shapeless, gooey figure descends from above, wearing a tuxedo t-shirt.
The creature—later identified as Meat Shield—contains moving human forms within it. One victim briefly pushes through the skin and screams before vanishing again. Meat Shield greets Templar: “So nice of you to join the dance party.” Battle on the Bridge:
Mantis Shrimp activates the backpack device, discovering it grants flight. A speedster abducts a bystander as a car phases through the bridge.
Manifester attempts to blink the dancers to safety but fails.
Templar shoots a nearby boom box to stop the music—unsuccessfully.
Manifester creates an illusion of silence, breaking the crowd’s trance.
Among the revelers, a new villain—Mosh Pit—is revealed. Combat Escalates: Meat Shield taunts: “You found my colleague: Mosh Pit!” Mosh Pit fires at Manifester but misses. Manifester retaliates with a psychic energy wave, knocking Mosh Pit unconscious. Templar shoots Mosh Pit’s weapon away—his bullet ricochets, striking Fire Cube (Molotov) as he approaches. Meat Shield slingshots himself off the bridge and flees. Mantis Shrimp drains hydrogen from the blimp to prevent explosion while Templar blasts incoming fireballs. Fire Cube retreats.
Automatic Man 2.0 intercepts police chatter confirming the gooey attacker’s name: Meat Shield.
Mantis Shrimp – Gains flight using the mysterious backpack; prevents a blimp explosion.
Templar – Uses precision shooting to neutralize threats and save civilians.
Larry Harry Jones – Disrupts the mind-controlled crowd through illusion and bravado.
Automatic Man 2.0 – Monitors communications, confirming villain identities and coordinating the team.
Meat Shield – A horrifying, goo-based entity containing live victims.
Mosh Pit – Ally of Meat Shield; uses sound and crowd frenzy as a weapon.
Fire Cube – Returns briefly before being driven off. This session marks the heroes’ first shift into Dimension 1, where subtle yet disturbing differences define their world—alternate leadership, infrastructure, and cultural echoes. The fight on the Buck O’Neil Bridge introduces new enemies tied to sound and flesh-based mutation, while surreal humor (Manifester’s reactions, Mantis’s impulsive heroism) tempers the dark tone. Dr. Goodfellow’s “Eureka!” and the bizarre suitcase hint at continuity between dimensions.(Note: this session and the next several are in Dimension 1.)Session 8: 11/12/23We exit the geodesic dome; overhear Goodfellow saying “eureka!” as we leave.
