It shoves its way into the bridge entrance, stopping traffic. Giant happy trout. Someone blacked out some of its teeth and wrote “I am a bomb” on it. It is on far side of bridge from us. Templar senses someone is on top of the bridge. In distance hear REO Speedwagon “Time for Me to Fly.” People hearing the music get out of their cars and dance. Music has menacing feel. Something begins lowering itself down from the top of the bridge like silly putty wearing clothes: tuxedo t-shirt. Is larger than normal person and has moving blobs within it. Has crazy eyes and greets Templar “so nice of you to join the dance party.” A blob pushes through skin and it’s a person who screams. Mantis puts on backpack. It gives him wings/power of flight. A couple turns into combat, someone runs past at hyperspeed, jumps up, car goes fuzzy focus; they grab someone out of the car and the car phases through the bridge. Manifester tries to use blink to create portals to transport dancers away from harm—fails. They fizzle out. Templar shoots boom box… the music did not stop. Manifester notes one of the revelers chuckles at the attempt to silence the music. Manifester creates illusion of no music, breaking the trance of the dancers. Manifester points out the baddie among the revelers. Gooey guy says “You found my colleague: Mosh Pit!” then swats at Automatic Man. In distance, see someone flying towards us, looks like Fire Cube. Mosh Pit pulls gun on Manifester but misses. Manifester blasts Mosh Pit with an energy wave, knocking him out. Templar shoots gun out of Mosh Pit’s hand, bullet ricochets to hit Fire Cube/Molotov. Gooey slingshots himself away. Mantis sucks the hydrogen out of the blimp as fireballs go at it, Templar blasting them out of the sky. Molotov runs away. Automatic Man hears police chatter: “Meat Shield” is gooey guy.

sessions/session-9.html.title: Session 9
sessions/session-9.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 11, 2022 Dimension: 1 A Familiar Enemy Returns: A local hero known as Blurry reports prior battles against Meat Shield, Mosh Pit, and Fire Cube, including a previous team-up with Templar in a church. This is the second time he’s killed Mosh Pit, but in earlier encounters, killing Mosh Pit caused people under his trance to fall into comas—some still remain comatose. Incoming Alert: Cell phones across the team buzz with the cryptic message: “Blurry 51-50 H H.”
Blurry contacts them, explaining that the comatose victims are being moved. He insists they must intervene despite warnings from his AI assistant, Jerry. The Supercar Unveiled: The group meets Blurry at a garage, where he proudly reveals Templar’s upgraded stealth Humvee—a combat-ready vehicle with retractable turret and an onboard AI. Jerry disapproves of the rescue mission.
Blurry believes Manifester can wake the coma victims through psychic means. Jerry detects three tactical troop carriers, warning that two are likely decoys. Highway Pursuit: In Templar’s Humvee, the heroes race after the transports. Blurry warns of a sniper on an overpass.
Templar fires but misses; Manifester creates an illusion of the Humvee being slightly offset, tricking the enemy’s aim. The illusion of the car exploding convinces their attackers they’ve been destroyed. Engagement with the Convoy: Templar closes in on the trucks.
Mantis Shrimp leaps onto the first vehicle’s roof as Khaki Tacs open fire.
Manifester uses a psychic blast—described as a “heat wave”—knocking one gunman unconscious. Templar commands the drivers over the PA: “Stop!” The trucks brake suddenly—throwing Mantis Shrimp off and sending him tumbling along the highway. Templar exits the Humvee, guns drawn, as soldiers emerge and return fire. Coordinated Combat: Manifester leaps from the car with theatrical mist and a grand gesture, attempting to conjure fire raining from the sky—fails, then hides behind the vehicle. Over comms, Blurry declares: “I’m about to go out of focus. I’m starting with the middle one.” Moments later, the middle truck phases, dropping its occupants onto the pavement. Blurry yells: “It’s not number 2!” Templar disables the fleeing third truck’s tire, slowing it down. Mantis Shrimp attempts to leap aboard but falls short—getting run over in the process. Templar rolls under the truck for cover, ricochets a bullet that pops another tire and incapacitates two Khaki Tacs. Mantis rips off the bumper in frustration. Manifester casts an illusion of the truck on fire, scattering the enemy troops. Rescue: Templar opens the truck’s rear compartment, revealing three unconscious people strapped to medical gurneys with monitors attached.
Manifester creates a calming mass illusion of quiet, which wakes them from their comas—confused but alive. The group loads them into Templar’s Humvee and escapes the scene. Jerry, surprised the plan actually succeeded, mutters his disbelief. Safehouse and the Resistance: Blurry directs them to his safehouse at 1580 E 19th Street, disguised as an autobody shop. Jerry quickly realizes this Templar is not from their dimension, identifying the heroes as off-worlders. They meet members of a resistance movement opposing a totalitarian Kansas City government: Cash is outlawed, replaced entirely by digital credits. FEMA and surveillance networks monitor all citizen movement. KC is effectively partitioned off from the rest of the U.S. Unexpected Call:
Manifester’s phone rings. The caller ID reads: “The Wife.” He looks at it and says: “I’m not going to pick that up.”
Templar – Takes command in tactical combat, rescues captives, and navigates interdimensional confusion.
Mantis Shrimp – Engages trucks physically, endures multiple impacts, and adds comic resilience.
Larry Harry Jones – Uses illusion and psychic force to control chaos, freeing coma victims.
Automatic Man 2.0 – Provides coordination, communications, and situational awareness (background role).
Blurry – New ally; can phase through matter, disrupt vehicles, and has ties to a local resistance.
Jerry – AI companion in Templar’s Humvee; pragmatic, dryly skeptical. Khaki Tacs – Armed paramilitary unit escorting comatose citizens. The Resistance – Underground movement opposing KC’s authoritarian rule in Dimension 1. The Wife – Identity unknown; contacts Manifester at session’s end. This session expands the Dimension 1 timeline, revealing a dystopian Kansas City under martial surveillance and digital currency control. Blurry introduces local stakes and history with familiar villains, suggesting dimensional echoes of earlier foes. The tone blends cinematic vehicular action with dark satire—“Jerry thinks it’s a bad idea” versus “I’m not going to pick that up.” The session closes on unease, resistance intrigue, and the unsettling realization that the heroes may not be able to return home easily.Session 9: 11/19/23 HERO COIN: ·       +3 to any roll ·       Reroll any D20 or effort roll ·       +2 stun or +2 hit points ·       Use power 1 level higher than you normally could ·       Give coin away Think of a personality quality to describe the character. +++ Other hero has fought Meat Shield, Mosh Pit, Molotov three times. He once fought them with Templar in a church. This is second time he’s killed Mosh Pit. When he killed MP before, some people who were under his trance went into comas and are still in them. Cell phones go off—“blurry 51-50 H H” “Wow, those people are being moved. Templar, Jerry got your car fixed. Lets get it.” New guy’s name is Blurry. They drop off blimp outside Freddie’s Trout House then head to garage with Blurry’s directions. See car with cover over it. Garage setup. Blurry is excited to show Templar the car. Pulls cover off to reveal super car: stealth’ed out Humvee with retractable turret, James Bond-style goodies. Starts up and computer console screen brings up “Jerry.” Jerry thinks bad idea to try to help the comatose people who are being moved; Blurry and he argue about whether to save them or just monitor the movement. Blurry thinks Manifester can get them out of the coma. Blurry explains comms will fall off as soon as he phases to use his powers. Jerry confirms 3 tactical looking troop-carrier vehicles carrying people; expect 2 are decoys. We leave in Templar’s Humvee. Blurry warns of someone setting up with weapon on an overpass. Templar misses with guns, but Manifester makes illusion that car is slightly off to the side from where it actually is. They shoot at it and Manifester makes it look like they were blown up. Templar catches up to the three trucks, pulls ahead of them. Mantis jumps onto roof of first one. The trucks spread out. Khahki Tacs lean out windows and aim guns at Mantis Manifester mind blasts one of the shooters: Ripple like a heat wave shoots through the air, shooter collapses dropping gun, skitters down the highway Vehicles bear down on Templar Templar has targeting system aim at drivers and PA system says to “Stop!” Vehicles slam on brakes. Mantis can’t hold on and flies off, tumbling along the ground unceremoniously. Templar brakes and turns car dramatically, then steps out guns drawn. People from the vehicle begin producing weaponry, poking out windows/hatches and some exiting and taking cover behind them. Manifester jumps out of the supercar with swirling mists and grand gesture. Attempts mass illusion for KTs of fireballs raining from sky to make them take cover; fails. With another swirling mist and cloud of smoke, he scurries behind the car. Blurry over comms says “I’m about to go out of focus. I’m starting with the middle one.” KTs begin firing Mantis and vehicle; not even close to hitting. Hit vehicle and no damage done. Templar advances on one of the side vehicles, shoot point blank into engine block and… does nothing. Mantis uppercuts the engine block and demolishes it. Second vehicle goes blurry and all KTs fall out onto the highway. We hear Blurry yell “It’s not number 2” Third vehicle squeals it tires, trying to take off. Templar blasts out it’s tire, slowing it down. They’re still driving on the rims. Mantis jumps towards fleeing vehicle, but falls just short, falling just in front of the back tire, which rolls over him. KTs open fire on Templar, who rolls underneath the truck for cover then shoots with ricochet to hits the other front tire and two KTs. Mantis attempts to pick up the vehicle; grabs the bumper and it rips right off. Manifester makes illusion that vehicle is on fire. They flee. Templar checks out the back of truck. There are three people locked in gurneys inside with medical monitors, unconscious. Manifester uses mass illusion on the comatose people of quiet. They almost immediately start to stir and open their eyes, completely disoriented and confused. We pack them into Templar’s vehicle and drive off. Jerry is annoyed and surprised that the mission worked. Seems to be family of Blurry. Blurry has a safehouse in autobody place near 19th and Vine. 1580 E 19th Street. Jerry quickly realizes Templar is not their Templar; sees Templar is not from this dimension. Meet ragtag group running a resistance to the government. In this reality, KC basically partitioned off. Cash is illegal; use digital currency only. FEMA is super involved. Loads of surveillance. Manifester’s phone rings – caller ID “The Wife” “I’m not going to pick that up.”

sessions/session-10.html.title: Session 10
sessions/session-10.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 11, 2022 Dimension: 1 Jerry’s Observation: Jerry becomes increasingly aware of the heroes’ off-world origins, confirming they are from an alternate universe.
His cold, logical demeanor contrasts with Blurry’s enthusiasm and risk-taking leadership. Manifester’s Celica on the News:
Manifester begins receiving frantic texts asking why his Celica is on the news—broadcast live in a low-speed police chase through Kansas City.
The driver is none other than Automatic Man 2.0, who appears disoriented and confused. [GM note: Automatic Man’s “training simulations” were based on Grand Theft Auto.] A Psychic Connection: Despite the distance, Manifester feels a telepathic link to the car’s CD player, suggesting his powers can extend through objects he’s emotionally bonded with. The Chase and the Pit Stop: The car is headed from River Market toward West Bottoms, driving erratically. Before pursuing, the group stops at Gates BBQ for food—an appropriately KC decision—then meanders after Automatic Man. They notice an ARIES vehicle tailing them but breaking off when they reach the West Bottoms. The Scene at 1104 Union Ave: The area is desolate. A Blackhawk helicopter lies on its side, smashed as though by blunt trauma. A massive magnetic crane looms nearby, holding Manifester’s Celica aloft by its undercarriage.
Automatic Man 2.0 is inside, seemingly paralyzed or exhausted, possibly due to the magnetic field. Smoke pours from the crane. Below it stands a heavyset figure in improvised armor, controlling the swirling debris around them with telekinetic or magnetic power. Templar detects multiple threats in surrounding buildings: 5th floor (right building): weapon being readied. 3rd floor (left building): chains clanking, possible captive. Ahead: a cyclone forming, pulling in rebar and debris. Combat Erupts:
Initiative Order: Templar, Manifester, Villains, Mantis Shrimp. Templar sets the Humvee to defense mode, bails out, and takes cover behind a burned-out car. Manifester teleports to the 4th floor of a nearby building. Automatic gunfire erupts toward Templar—bullets hit the wreckage but miss him. The cyclone intensifies; the crane groans under strain. Mantis Shrimp steps into the swirling debris, catches a flying radiator, and begins bending it into a weapon while trying to talk the armored foe down. The enemy responds by flipping him off. Templar’s Precision Shot: Hearing a gunman cock a weapon, Templar fires through the sound—his bullet hits the shooter in the mouth, dropping him through the window. Both the gun and body are pulled into the debris cyclone. Manifester’s Interference: From above, Manifester spots the armored foe clearly and realizes he’s controlling the debris field. He attempts to impose an illusion of blindness, but fails. The crane’s motor begins to overheat and will fail in three rounds. The Cyclone Grows: The stocky armored villain tightens control over the debris, creating a funnel cloud. Mantis is swept up and suspended in midair, the radiator pole fusing magnetically to the crane’s dish. (Ion pack rule reminder: grants flight for 1d4 rounds, then 1d4 rounds of recovery.) Distress Call: From the building on the left, Templar hears a woman crying, “Help me!” followed by a man’s warning: “Woman, don’t get them involved—they’ll just get killed.” Templar starts climbing to intervene. The Cyclone Strikes Back: The armored foe launches the debris storm toward Templar. A corpse smashes into him, dealing minor damage (4 points), and he’s sucked into the cyclone, spinning helplessly. Mantis clings desperately to the embedded radiator pole beneath the suspended Celica. End Scene: Mantis climbs higher, grabs the car frame, and tries to wrench it free from the magnet. The vehicle only shifts position—now driver side up. Inside, Automatic Man tumbles, his stunned face slamming against the passenger window—right next to Mantis. Mantis ends the session with 6 stun points, the storm raging and the crane beginning to fail.
Templar – Tactical precision; identifies threats, eliminates a gunman, and braves the cyclone.
Larry Harry Jones – Teleports into position, manipulates the field with illusions, but fails key psychic rolls.
Mantis Shrimp – Physically engages the debris storm, attempts negotiation and heroics while midair.
Automatic Man 2.0 – Found incapacitated within Manifester’s Celica, likely disabled by the magnetic field.
Blurry – Mentioned but off-screen this session; his team remains in contact.
Jerry – Coldly rational AI, recognizes the team’s extradimensional status. Armored Villain (unnamed) – Controls debris via magnetic or telekinetic force; central antagonist of the scene. Unknown Captives – Possibly civilians or prisoners; one female voice heard pleading for help. This session blends cinematic chaos with dark humor and heavy foreshadowing. The heroes face a magnetic storm of chaotic forces, literal and figurative: dimensional dislocation, machine influence, and psychic overstimulation. Manifester’s growing psychic connection to technology, especially his Celica, hints at deeper cross-dimensional resonance. The magnetic crane, the storm, and the armored foe set up a high-stakes cliffhanger—leaving the team battered, disoriented, and still mid-battle.Session Ten: 12/10/23 [Jerry is smart, able to detect that we are from an alternate universe. Jerry cold and calculating; Blurry takes more risks, is enthusiastic, leader-like but not ranked.] Manifester is getting repeated texts asking why his car is on the news. TV turns on low-speed chase following Manifester’s Celica, Automatic Man is driving. [Automatic Man was run through computer simulations to develop his abilities and… he used Grand Theft Auto as his simulator] Manifester can feel a connection with the CD player despite being many miles away. Car is in River Market, headed towards West Bottoms somewhat erratically and badly. We stop at Gates for food before heading out to intercept Automatic Man. We meander towards him. An ARIES starts following us. As we get into West Bottoms, we pass barrels w graffiti of happy face with horns, ARIES vehicles stop following once we get there. We get to about 1104 Union Ave. Area is desolate. A Blackhawk helicopter is crashed on its side, smashed by blunt objects. A large magnetic crane is raised with Manifester’s celica attached to the magnet. Automatic Man is inside, looks exhausted, perhaps due to the magnetic field. Seems stunned. Nobody seems to be operating crane but smoke is coming out of it, not in great shape. Just past crane is a heavyset person wearing makeshift armor. In buildings can hear people scurrying about. Templar detects movement on fifth floor of building to right, hears sound of automatic weapon cocking. In building on left, third floor, hears clanking of chains as a person has it on them or are chained up. Ahead hear wind swirling near the heavyset person, catching dust, small objects, rebar. An 8-foot horizontal cylinder of air begins to form. Mantis rolls down window and shouts towards heavyset person. Templar hears someone ducking down and cocking gun. He has supercar gun target the source of noise. (Order: Templar, Manifester, villains, Mantis) Templar turns car into defense mode and bales out, heading towards left parking garage, crouches behind a burnt out car. Manifester teleports up into building at fourth floor. Someone begins firing automatic weapon at Templar, missing but hitting the burnt out car. Wind baton is building up with larger and larger objects. Smoke coming out of crane is picking up. Mantis walks into the cylinder and catches a radiator from the debris, begins straightening it. Tries to talk to the heavyset person in armor, but they just flick him off. Templar shoots back at person shooting toward him; shot through the mouth, staggers and falls through the window to the ground. He (and the gun) begins churning in the debris field. Manifester runs to the end of the building. He has a good view of the crane and guy in armor; can tell he’s controlling the debris. Crane motor looks like it’s going to go in 3 turns. Manifester attempts to give stocky armor guy illusion of blindness; fails. Stocky turns the debris into more of a funnel cloud. Mantis gets pulled up into the cloud. The metal of the pole Mantis uncoiled from radiator sticks to the magnetic dish. [Ion pack: have flight for 1d4 rounds, then takes 1d4 to recover] From building on left, Templar hears woman’s voice saying “help me! Help me!” and masculine voice saying “woman don’t get them involved. They’ll just get killed” Templar begins climbing to move into the building Manifester now attempts to give stocky guy illusion of sensory deprivation. Chunky armor guy sends cyclone towards Templar. Dead body smacks into Templar giving 4 pts damage and he’s pulled into cyclone, spinning through the air. Leaves Mantis hanging from the rod in the air. Mantis climbs up the radiator pole to underneath the car, grabs the frame and yanks in attempt to dislodge car, fails. The car only turns, still attached to magnet, driver side up. Automatic Man falls into the passenger side, his stunned face hits the window right next to Mantis’ head. [Mantis ends session with 6 stun points]

sessions/session-11.html.title: Session 11
sessions/session-11.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 11, 2022 Dimension: 1 Templar vs. Windy: Templar continues to swirl within the storm, firing at the armored wind-controller (dubbed Windy). His shot lands true, slamming Windy into the ground and breaking the cyclone apart. He throws a rappel line onto a nearby building and swings toward the collapsing battle zone. Manifester’s Attempt:
Larry Harry Jones tries to create an illusion of Automatic Man 2.0’s Celica falling onto Windy, but the illusion fails. Windy’s Escape: Windy uses gusts of air to hurl himself into a second-story window of a nearby building. Mantis Shrimp’s Legal Interlude:
Mantis Shrimp’s cell phone rings—his lawyer Paul Hood is calling about his ongoing dispute with ARIES. Paul also mentions that “Deadpool” (possibly a codename or alias) is looking for Mantis—and he’s riding a Vespa. Tourists Arrive: A loudspeaker blares from a passing Mark Sargent Reality Tour bus: “The government thinks they can keep lying to us! First they said the Earth is round—now they say superheroes are real!” Tourists see Mantis Shrimp and exclaim he’s real; Mark insists he’s “an animatronic.” The bus later flees after witnessing him catch a falling car. Catching the Celica: The crane’s motor fails—the Celica plummets. Mantis leaps beneath it, catching the falling car in a dramatic show of strength. Passersby cheer as the bus speeds off in panic.
Mantis gently places Automatic Man 2.0 into the car, covers him with a jacket, and then jetpacks toward the building Windy entered. Templar’s Ascent: Templar leaps from a burnt-out car onto an awning and heads for the second floor, where he hears a woman calling for help. Manifester’s Encounter: Inside, Manifester finds a woman in a harness chained to a pillar. When she spots him, she turns invisible, though the chain and harness remain visible. Manifester quips, “Looks like I’m interrupting something… I didn’t realize that club had moved here.” The chain retracts around the pillar—its end unseen. Bulltoad Appears: From the shadows emerges a mutant hybrid of human, toad, and bull, who bellows, “You shouldn’t have come here. Now Bulltoad’s gonna have to kick your ass!” Manifester psychically blasts him, but Bulltoad retaliates—goring Manifester and hurling him through a window onto an awning. “Carmelita, you know I only keep you chained up because of certain masculine insecurities,” Bulltoad mutters. Templar’s Counterattack: Templar shoots Bulltoad mid-rant, instantly knocking him out, splattering goo across the room—and across Manifester. “You killed him! You killed him, you horrible monster!” Carmelita screams, still restrained. Mantis rockets up toward the roof in search of Windy but instead encounters a new foe made of living concrete. The invisible woman (Carmelita) fires energy blasts at Templar and misses. Manifester tries a psychic counterattack, but also misses. Concrete bellows, “You’ll have to do better than that!” He slams the floor, collapsing it. Templar and Mantis both plummet to the lower level. Concrete then melds into the ceiling to pursue them. The Climactic Blow: Mantis shrinks down, then suddenly resizes mid-punch, uppercutting the Concrete villain straight through the ceiling. The sound of collapsing masonry echoes moments later. The heroes stabilize Bulltoad (still alive) and free Carmelita, leaving her restrained but safe.
They prepare to exit the No-Go Zone, where Khaki Tacs are stationed at the perimeter. Manifester disguises their vehicles as Khaki Tac transports using illusion. They successfully slip past security undetected. In the Celica, the magnetized CD player now plays “Give It Up” by KC & The Sunshine Band. Inside the glovebox, they find a fancy costume catalogue addressed to a mansion on Ward Parkway—their next lead.
Templar: Marksman and acrobat; eliminates Bulltoad and leads tactical movement.
Larry Harry Jones: Illusionist and psychic; discovers Carmelita, engages Bulltoad, and later facilitates escape.
Mantis Shrimp: Strength and agility; rescues Automatic Man and defeats Concrete in a cinematic knockout.
Automatic Man 2.0: Unconscious for most of the encounter, but rescued from the Celica wreck. Carmelita: Invisible woman, formerly chained captive of Bulltoad. Bulltoad: Mutant villain (bull/toad hybrid); defeated by Templar. Windy: Armored wind-controller; escaped early in the fight. Concrete: Living stone powerhouse; smashed through ceiling by Mantis Shrimp.
Paul Hood: Mantis Shrimp’s persistent and possibly overworked lawyer. Mark Sargent: Flat Earth tour guide; witnesses Mantis’s heroism but remains unconvinced. The “Mark Sargent Reality Tours” scene—perfect Kansas City absurdity meets meta-comedy. Mantis catching the Celica mid-fall—a classic comic-book splash page moment. Manifester’s line to the invisible woman: “Didn’t realize that club moved here.” The CD player humor—Mantis’s Celica now permanently tied to Kansas City’s disco heritage. Session 11: 12/17/23 Templar swirling in the whirlwind, shoots at armor guy. Hits him, blasting him to the ground. Whirlwind starts to dissipate. Templar throws a rappel line onto the tallest building and swings towards Windy. Manifester attempts to create an illusion of the Celica falling onto Windy, but fails. Windy uses wind to fly into the second floor of the shorter building. Mantis’ cellphone ring. Talks to Paul Hood, his lawyer, asking about fight with ARIES. He says Deadpool ???? is looking for Mantis, riding his Vespa. Can hear loudspeaker of someone making announcement—the government thinks they can keep lying to us. First they said Earth is round, now they say superheroes are real. Mark Seargent Reality Tours on side of bus we see. Hear tourists saying “Mantis Shrimp is real!” Mark S says “No no, that’s animatronic” Mantis opens passenger door, and Automatic Man falls to the ground. Mantis drops down and pulls AM out of the area where car might fall. Templar moves across street, leaps from a burnt-out car onto an awning towards Wind Guy and the woman calling for help. Manifest teleports into the other building, second floor. Sees a woman wearing a harness with chain attached. She sees him then turns invisible, but harness and chain are still visible. “Looks like I’m interrupting something… I didn’t realize that club had moved here.” Chain goes back around a pillar and can’t see the end. They hear the engine of the crane give out. Car is falling. Mantis runs under and catches the car. People on the bus say “He’s not animatronic! Mantis Shrimp is real.” The tour bus quickly drives away with Mark grumbling. …[new initiative] Manifester sees Human-Toad-Bull combo. He says “You shouldn’t have come here. Now Bulltoad is gonna have to kick your ass!” Manifester blasts Bulltoad with psychic blast. Bulltoad comes bounding towards Manifester, jiggly and gores Manifester, pitching him out window onto awning. “Woman, see what you made me do? Carmelita you know I only keep you chained up because of certain masculine insecurities.” Templar shoots Bulltoad, and takes him down to 0; frog goo splatters all over Manifester. “You killed him! You killed him, you horrible monster!” Mantis puts AM into the Celica gently, covers him with a jacket, then jet-packs to where he saw Windy-Armor flee. Energy blast from invisible woman flies past Templar, who is now visible. Manifester psychic blasts at woman but misses. Bulltoad is breathing but incapacitated. Templar runs towards woman, she blasts at him but misses again, again impacting the building. Mantis doesn’t see, but hear and feel wind picking up. Mantis has no idea where he is. Manifester attempts to make an illusion of Khaki Tacs storming the building, but fails. Templar tackles her. Zip ties her. Mantis hears a rumbling sound but not soon enough. Gets sucker-punched, 15 damage, flies skittering across the floor. Whoever punched him descends from the ceiling, looks like living concrete in human form. Mantis heads towards new threat, shrinking down. (+6 defense) Manifester misses with another psychic blast at concrete guy. Templar shoots him, but bullet appears to bounce off him. Concrete says “You’re gonna have to do better than that,” and smacks the ground and damages the ground. Mantis and Templar both fall through floor to the level below. Concrete reaches up and absorbs himself up into the ceiling. Mantis flies up through the hole in the floor back to the second floor. Manifester psychic blasts concrete guy for 1 stun dmg. Templar throws out rope and climbs back up to second floor. Concrete swings at Mantis and misses. Mantis swings back, unshrinking, uppercutting and smashing concrete up and out through the ceiling and much later, there’s the sound of concrete falling. Situation resolved; they set Carmelita back up and reassure her the Bulltoad is ok. They loosen but do not remove her bounds. Now they need to get past the Khaki Tacts on the outskirts of the No-Go Zone. Manifester gets into the Celica and the CD player, scrambled by the magnet, now plays “Give It Up” by KC & The Sunshine Band. Manifester then disguises vehicles as Khaki Tac vehicles, and they slip past without issue. In Celica they find a fancy costume catalogue, addressed to a house on Ward Parkway—basically a mansion.

sessions/session-12.html.title: Session 12
sessions/session-12.html.description:
In-Game Date: April 11, 2022 Dimension: 1 Back at the Hotel: The captive The Master now appears human (resembling actor William Smith). Mantis Shrimp abruptly shifts into his baseline identity Claude Crevette, losing most powers. The Master is rattled and fears he won’t survive the night. “Dave” the Master:
Larry Harry Jones successfully implants the belief that the Master’s name is “Dave.” “Dave” bargains for release after he fixes Vicki’s memories and provides a write-up on The Gnome. Disguises Go Awry: Manifester’s illusion disguises accidentally make the team look like Macho Man Randy Savage clones. At The Majestic:
In the crowded, KT-heavy club, Maxwell Manning rails against opening for a Bon Jovi cover band, The Ardent Natural Philosophers of BJ.
Off-duty Khaki Tacs drink and mourn two colleagues killed earlier. Templar learns they expect a coming “advantage” (supersoldier serum; internal comms), gleaned by “Dave” via mind read. Leandra Sighting:
Leandra is present in a red cocktail dress; private watch/text exchange with Manifester confirms covert coordination. Opening Act — Dr. Fervid & Co.:
Dr. Fervid (frontman) introduces Master of the Hunt (guitar/axe), Hannah the Hammer (drums/dulcimer), The Banshees (backup singers), and Sammy Von Newman (AM look-alike on bass). They launch into “Bad Medicine.” Vicki’s Memory Fix:
Downstairs, “Dave” removes Vicki’s implanted false memory (2–3 minutes, traumatic). She collapses sobbing; Automatic Man 2.0 escorts her back to friend Dianne. MOLES Breach / Music Control: A MOLES darkness mass bursts through a wall. The band’s enchantment freezes civilians with a looping “Livin’ on a Prayer” chorus, and Banshees push KTs toward violence. Countermoves:
Templar shoots the amp power—music softens. He threatens the band. AM’s blast craters a wall (no injuries). Dr. Fervid eye-blasts at Templar. Manifester mutes the singers with illusion, snapping KTs out of it; the Banshees notice the interference. AM and Maxwell spark a “hold hands” rush to the exits, helping civilians and KTs flee. Fight & Flight: Blows traded: Manifester stuns Master of the Hunt; Templar wounds Dr. Fervid (revealing a more diabolical form). Leandra (invisible) zaps a Banshee (“You’re welcome, dear.”) Hannah and The Banshees escape through a glowing banner. Dr. Fervid sings “We’ll Meet Again,” blasts AM, then also jumps through the banner. Automatic Man 2.0 decks Master of the Hunt, killing him. The banner remains glowing as the scene ends.
Mantis Shrimp / Claude Crevette – Temporarily depowered; later engages in the club fight and backs up Leandra.
Templar – Intel-gathering among KTs; decisive shots to reduce the band’s control; engages villains.
Larry Harry Jones – Rebrands The Master as “Dave,” orchestrates disguises, mutes the Banshees’ song, and coordinates evac.
Automatic Man 2.0 – Protects civilians (Vicki), trades fire with Dr. Fervid, and finishes Master of the Hunt.
The Master (“Dave”) – Cooperative under duress; performs the Vicki fix; manipulative but fearful.
Dr. Fervid – Band leader with eye-beams and reality-warping songcraft; escapes via banner.
Hannah the Hammer – Drummer/dulcimer; leaps into the banner.
The Banshees – Sonic enchanters with knives; two throw at Manifester; all flee through the banner.
Master of the Hunt – Guitar/axe berserker; killed by Automatic Man 2.0.
M.O.L.E.S. – Breach the club to “rescue” the Master; presence heightens chaos.
Maxwell Manning – Outraged bandleader, helps lead the crowd to safety.
Vicki – Reporter whose false memory is removed; escorted by AM to Dianne. Off-duty Khaki Tacs – Armed crowd; briefly puppeted by the band’s music. Deal struck: release “Dave” after Vicki is restored and he delivers a full dossier on The Gnome. KT chatter: supersoldier serum and internal comms program underway. The glowing banner functions as a portal; several band members escaped through it. Leandra operates covertly; tech glasses noted. Session 12: 1/20/24 Return to hotel room; Master still there and restrained but now looks like different now—looks like actor William Smith instead of weird bulbous headed person. Mantis feels weird and then changes into Claude Crevette, his original appearance and without most of his powers. Master is perturbed but hiding it bc he’s afraid of us. He says it’s highly likely he won’t survive the evening. He’s wondering once he’s removed the false memory, what does he do next. Manifester decides to call Master “Dave.” Creates illusion to make him believe his name is actually Dave, which succeeds. Dave admits there was no agreement, but he’s hoping we’ll release him. Leans on his theme of persecution. We agree to release him if he does his job, but also gives us a writeup of everything he knows about The Gnome. Manifester creates illusion to disguise them, but accidentally makes them look basically exactly like Macho Man Randy Savage ---we head to the Majestic--- We come upon Maxwell Manning arguing with someone “The First Laws are never going to open for a fucking Bon Jovi cover band!” When he sees Automatic Man he comes over “Ian! Tell these fuckwads will never open for this fucking hack act!” A bunch of hipster kids waiting for the doors to open defend the band: The Ardent Natural Philosophers of BJ. A guy comes out looking like Jermaine from Flight of the Concords and says “Maxwell, I respect what you do. We’ll open for you!” Inside, Majestic crawling with off duty Khaki Tacs; off duty, drinking, but armed. Act will be downstairs. We overhear Khaki Tacs having get together bc 2 colleagues were killed today fighting anomalies. Mantis asks Manifester if there’s anything he can do to get rid of the “brownies.” Manifester attempts to make illusion of call to send all available KTs to the airport; fails. Templar sits down in the midst of the KTs and says “what’s up guys.” Chit chats with them. Overhears they will be getting an advantage soon. “George, they don’t need to know about that!” Master – uses mind reading to discover they have a supersoldier serum plus an internal commlink. Vicki walks in with a companion. We head downstairs. Stage to left, bar to right. More hipsters. More KTs. Fans of the First Laws (16 to 96 years old, lots of dusters, trenchcoats, cutoff shorts, almost all wearing Chuck Taylor All-Stars, some in sunglasses). Also attractive woman with dark hair in red cocktail who visibly reacts at the sight of Manifester—it’s Leandra. She speaks into her watch. He gets text message: “Dear why are you here, and what have you done with your hair.” She’s flirting with a nerdy looking computer guy. He texts back “Incognito. Act naturally. I’ll explain it all later. PS do you have any cash on you.” She texts back “Just cards. Low profile. Good idea.” On stage there’s a banner that’s ornate, Celtic looking symbol plus the name of the band. Vicki and friend are at a table. Leandra is wearing glasses; they look polarized or high tech. Jermaine-looking guy comes out. Introduces self as Dr Fervid. “Master of the Hunt on guitar” antler hat guy. Woman in green clothing with hat partly covering eyes “Hannah the hammer on drums and dulcimer” three women in dresses “And the banshees backing me up” then finally “our final member gets in scraps and he’s got himself killed again on the I-??? bridge, but don’t worry he will join us again soon. For now, we have Sammy Von Newman.” Guy looks like a smaller version of Automatic Man. Then they break into a version of Bad Medicine Maxwell is disgusted by this “You see why we will never open for this crap? But Ian, your younger brother is a pretty good bass player.” Midway through set, Vicki heads towards the back, towards bathroom. Manifester follows her with Dave, Mantis, and Manifester. Templar sits at bar eating steak, watching over them. Manifester and Dave talking: Dave admits it will take 2-3 minutes and will cause her some significant trauma. Manifester makes an illusion of a janitor mopping up vomit; it works but on the ceiling. Dave quickly undoes his prior work. Vicki drops to the floor sobbing. Manifester drops the illusion and walks out of the area. Automatic man moves to check on Vicki. She pulls away from him. He asks her “Vicki are you ok. Are you ok. Are you ok Vicki.” “No, I don’t know what’s happened to me. It’s like a terrible dream. Help me back to my friend Dianne.” AM takes her through the club to the bar. Templar hears grumbling, scraping, scratching sound behind wall opposite stage. Templar looks at Dave and says “Your friends?” “Those foolish loyal creatures! Are they here to rescue me” Wall crumbles and a blob of darkness emerges as the band continues to play. Templar turns to KTs, “That looks like your job, boys.” Initiative roll Manifester urges people to leave. Some people do move that way. Mantis tells Dave “IF you’ve done your homework, you’re free to go.” He gives paper re: The Gnome and runs towards the MOLES. Band keeps playing over and over again “ooooh, we’re halfway there. Ooooh, we’re halfway there…” and everyone that’s a normal person is frozen in place. The three ladies start singing “Shot through the heart!” and KTs start to point guns at the hipsters. Templar looks for power source for amplifiers and shoots it. Music gets quieter, still playing but not amplified. Templar then points toward the band, “Stop playing or you’re next.” When music collapses, big guitarist with no sleeves and antlers on his head hops off stage and starts wielding guitar like an axe and blades pop out. Automatic Man attempts to blast him with energy blast, it hits the wall making a major explosion but injuring no one. Hannah the Hammer moves to take cover behind dulcimer stand. Dr Fervid shoots green energy out his eyes at Templar. Manifester attempts illusion to mute the singing; succeeds. KTs shake their heads and are stunned by their own behavior. The Banshees see it and know Manifester interfered. Automatic Man with Maxwell together continue to sing the next line “Take my hand and we’ll make it I swear!” Mantis starts a chain of holding hands. The hipsters and khaki tacs begin grabbing hands and bolting towards the stairs. Hannah the Hammer hits dulcimers and banner above band starts to glow. Dr Fervid fires a blast at Automatic Man, dealing 5 pts damage. The Banshees pull knives from their outfits. Mantis only sees Leandra turn invisible and hit a banshee with an energy blast (he later gets a text “You’re welcome, dear”). Other two miss when throwing knives at Manifester. Master of the Hunt swings at AM but misses. Sammy tries to punch Dr Fervid but misses. Manifester mind blasts Master of the Hunt; 3 pts stun damage. He falls to one knee. Templar shoots green eyes (Dr Fervid) for 4 pts. His appearance changes, looks less human and more diabolical. Master’s voice “Thank you, thank you my friends. Not just you, MOLES, you foolish friends. Thank you for coming to get me.” AM blasts Master of the Hunt, misses. Manifester mind blasts Hannah. Mantis heads over towards Leandra, shoots Hannah doing 6 dmg. Hannah says “We should flee,” then runs and jumps into the banner, disappearing. Two banshees grab the third, then also flee through the banner. Dr Fervid begins singing “We’ll meeeeet again! Don’t know where… don’t know when…” He then blasts AM for 3 more pts damage. Templar shoots at him, missing and Dr Fervid jumps through the banner. Master of the Hunt stands, staggering. Automatic Man smashes him with a fist, punches him so hard antlers fly off his head and driving him into the floor. He expires. Vicki and her friend escape upstairs. The banner is still glowing… [end session]

sessions/session-13.html.description:
In-Game Date: ≈ April 19, 2022 Dimension: 1 Aftermath at the Club: Sammy Von Newman collects biological samples from the fallen Master of the Hunt. Leandra & Manifester:
Larry Harry Jones learns he and Leandra are professional thieves/con artists; he also preaches, and followers often report “visions” of his sermons. Dimension-1 Civic Climate: Cash is being phased out for a government debit-card system. Leandra is trying to steal the code tied to this system to create a never-ending debit card. Templar’s Reputation & Lead:
In this timeline, the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception suffered heavy damage; a priest died and Templar is blamed (possibly due to Meat Shield). Templar meets Marvin, who points him to a soup kitchen/shelter and later to Grand Avenue Temple. Notes & Hooks from “Dave” (The Master):
“Dave” provides notes on The Gnome and The Fiddler, plus leads: New ARIES project to be run at Hangar 50. Natural Philosophers expected at Pecks Building, 1099 Baltimore Ave. Reference to a hidden depot disguised as a fireworks stand; rumor of N. Korean invasion; questions why the Fiddler needs so much power. Personal aside: he feels kinship with Mantis, but is terrified of “your friend with the gun.” Claude’s Dojo subplot:
Mantis Shrimp maintains a dojo in River Market; rivalry set up for a public showdown with Hipster Deadpool’s dojo. Jimbo Shrump assists. Forensics Thread:
Prior DNA testing on a sulfur-based “monster” shows no DNA for the creature; collateral DNA points to potential relatives Lee & Sara McClauren (MoDOC) and Tom McClauren (a felon) — Tom is visibly Jerry. Grand Avenue Temple — Delphi: Guided by Marvin, the team meets Delphi (paper-stacked office, lemonade/carrots). He says Councilman Eric Bunch remains jailed despite the reporter’s recantation and urges a covert interview. He supplies David Bell’s photo (Bunch’s attorney), jail floorplans, and entry procedure. Payment offered: $10k (Templar) / $7.5k (Mantis). Jail Infiltration: Disguises: Manifester as Andy Reid; Mantis with a Don Johnson mullet; Templar (unspecified). They pass the metal detectors with tiny/small/large energy guns and reach 5th floor.
Eric Bunch explains his automatic writing power: at an ionic power-plant meeting he compulsively recorded details about an out-of-place attendee — The Fiddler — including the machine schematic and motive. He hid the notes at home; he now senses they’re in Sen. Josh Hawley’s Western MO office. Alarm & Escape: When David Bell arrives, Manifester’s illusion stutters (for a second they all look like Richard Nixon). Guard alerts trigger, so Manifester casts a jail-on-fire illusion and Templar pulls the fire alarm. During the evac, Manifester’s disguise turns the team into Village People archetypes. They ultimately leave Bunch behind (reluctant to flee).
Outside, Automatic Man 2.0 is disguised as Bunch; they swap in the commotion and head for Hawley’s office. Office Breach (Hawley & Greitens): At the building, front desk refuses access. Manifester twice portals — first misplacing it outside, then successfully into the office, where Josh Hawley and Eric Greitens are present. Combat: Hawley grabs a shotgun and fires (miss). Greitens seizes a Civil War sword and strikes Mantis (2 dmg). Mantis flips Hawley’s desk, then smashes the shotgun away. Templar zipties Hawley. Manifester mind blasts Greitens (down). A floor safe is revealed; two armored guards enter but retreat when Templar commands. Mantis rips open the safe: mummified hand, handgun, simple dagger, four gold bars, laminated papers. The team portals out (after a misfire to 60 floors up) disguised as cleaning staff. Return & Reset: At the jail, an exterior hole ~5 floors up lets them slip Bunch back inside (Mantis carries him up while still “Village People” disguised). Findings: Notes identify Fiddler = Mike “Madman” Markham; his device contacts other dimensions to snag superbeings and bring them here. Items from the safe are secured.
Templar — Social engineering, intel gathering, commands guards, zipties Hawley.
Larry Harry Jones — Illusions/portals (fire/evac; Village People; cleaning staff), mind blast on Greitens.
Mantis Shrimp — Leads on Gnome/Fiddler; dojo subplot; desk-lift and safe-rip; assists Bunch swap/return.
Automatic Man 2.0 — Runs the Bunch swap; support/escort.
The Fiddler (aka Mike “Madman” Markham) — Designing a cross-dimensional superbeing snare; needs large power draw. ARIES / Hangar 50 — New project site. The Natural Philosophers — Planning return to Pecks Building. Khaki Tacs — Ongoing enforcement presence.
Leandra — Con artist/tech thief; target: debit-card system code.
The Master (“Dave”) — Provides notes and leads.
Sammy Von Newman — Collects MotH samples. Marvin — Street sweeper and source for Templar. Delphi — Grand Avenue Temple contact; plans the jail approach. Eric Bunch — Councilman with automatic writing; notes stolen to Hawley office. David Bell — Bunch’s attorney (identity used as cover). Josh Hawley & Eric Greitens — Encountered and neutralized during office breach.
Jerry — Identified via forensic family link (Tom McClauren). Hangar 50 (ARIES): project start. Pecks Building (1099 Baltimore): Natural Philosophers rendezvous. Hidden depot (fireworks stand cover). Debit-card system exploit (Leandra’s target). Cathedral incident: Templar’s blame and Meat Shield’s comment. Dojo showdown: Claude vs. Hipster Deadpool. Session 13: 2/3/24 Sammy collects bio samples from Master of the Hunt. Manifester discusses with Leandra enough to learn she AND HE are professional thieves/conartists. He also sometimes preaches on the side. Followers often have “visions” of his sermons. We are in a district where government is increasingly trying to make cash illegal, but it’s not working well. Government is making a debit card system. Leandra is trying to steal the code connected to debit for a never-ending-debit-card. Templar would learn that in this timeline there was massive damage at the Cathedral of the Emaculate Conception, the padre is dead and Templar is blamed for it. Meatshield had said something referencing this event, suggesting he accidentally did kill the priest. Templar meets “Marvin” a street sweeper with info who gives him info about a soup kitchen and shelter. Mantis has notes from The Master (Dave) about The Gnome. Mantis has a dojo in River Market. At some point Manis will need to have a public martial competition showdown against Hipster Deadpool’s dojo. Jimbo Shrump is assistant at Mantis’ dojo. Dave’s notes on Fiddler…[I missed a lot of this… hidden depot looks like fireworks stand. Unconfirmed N. Korean invasion rumor. Why does he need so much power?] “though we are different in may ways, I feel you and I are natural friends, though I am terrified of your friend with the gun.” Also knows new Aries project will be run at Hanger 50. He also discovered the Natural Philosophers were going to go back to Pecks Building at 1099 Baltimore Ave. Templar learns testing of DNA from much earlier—no apparent DNA from monster that attacked people. Chemically that being is sulfur based, not carbon based. There was DNA in sample presumably from person fighting the creature, but didn’t have DNA on any known database; however, there were some people who might be relatives – Lee & Sara McClauren (both members of Mo Dept of Corrections) and Tom McClauren (who is felon). When see pics, Tom is clearly Jerry. It's about April 19. Marvin finds Templar and encourages him to go the Grand Avenue Temple, bringing his allies. We go. Inside table is setup for soup kitchen. There’s wraparound balcony then stairs leading to an office. Marvin takes us up to the office. Middle aged, slightly overweight guy sitting at desk--Delphi. He talks like he knows Templar. Office is filled with papers, filing cabinets that require ladders. He offers lemonade or carrot juice. He notes that Councilman Bunch is still in custody despite reporter recanting her testimony, but he should be getting out soon. They think now’s the best time to talk to him. Shows us pics of David Bell, Mr. Bunch’s attorney. Suggests we pose as David Bell to interview Mr. Bunch to determine why this elaborate conspiracy was carried out against him. Also gives pics showing internal layout of jail. Describes the procedure for getting in. Delphi thinks Eric Bunch must have some very important information but why not kill him? Questioned by Mantis, he offers $10k and Mantis $7,500. Templar and Mantis bring 1 tiny, 1 small, and 1 large energy gun which we know go through metal detectors. Manifester makes himself look like Andy Reid. Mantis puts on a Don Johnson-like mullet wig. Templar ?? Manifester makes a passable illusion that we’re who we say we are. We head in. They have us sign in on visitors log. We go through metal detector. Head up to fifth floor. We go right. There’s someone to open reinforced glass bulkhead doors, 2 sets. Then go into room with metal desk and chairs. Can see guard through the glass. The intercom system doesn’t work properly; guard gestures who you’re here for. Write it on paper. Then eventually after about 15 minutes later they bring in Eric Bunch in orange croks and prison clothes. He’s excited to see us, “do you think the judge will change his decision.” Manifester talks about it with him, convinces him to tell him story again about what’s going on. Bunch has anomalous power. He writes and writes, and it includes things he can’t possibly know. The City has company wanting to build another ionic power plant. Didn’t understand why they needed it. At a meeting with the company, there was a guy seemed out of place, looked like he shopped at army surplus, round glasses. Everyone’s talking about the power plant. During meeting power kicks in, he starts scribbling away feverishly. Tries to hide it but doesn’t do it well; ended up getting info on that guy—he was The Fiddler. Lots of details in there that I can’t remember, but I had his name, why they wanted power plant, schematic for machine he was trying to design. In that moment I knew everything about the machine… I hid them in my house. But they’re gone now, I’m sure of it. I can sense where they are, they’re at the Western MO office for Senator Josh Hawley. Mantis and Manifester attempt to get pen from Bunch, but don’t succeed. I don’t remember what the machine does, but it’s why they need the power plant. I excused myself, but I didn’t do a good job. I felt like I was being watched every day until I was arrested. As we’re trying to leave, Bunch looks over Manifester’s shoulder and says “What the fuck?!” Manifester “Is my brother here again?” We see David Bell approaching. Manifester attempts to reinforce the illusion but fails. For just a second, all three of us look like Richard Nixon. Guard watching us in the pod notices and pushes an alert. Mantis hides under the table. Manifester tries to generate illusion as far reaching as possible that jail is on fire. Templar pulls fire alarm. Everyone is convinced. Initiative: Templar, Guards, Mantis, Manifester Templar bangs on the door “There’s a fire, idiots! Let us out!” Master control hears and opens the heavy doors. We make it back to the elevator, get in with Eric Bunch. Guards don’t get in bc THERE’S A FIRE (illusion). As heading down, Manifester attempts to make us look like firemen, but instead makes us look like the Village People. Mantis: motorcycle guy. Templar: Sailor. Manifester: cop or cowboy. Eric Bunch: construction worker. Bunch is reluctant to leave. We leave him behind. Automatic Man has been in the car this whole time. Manifester disguises AM as Eric Bunch, and we swap the two in the commotion of the “fire.” Then head to Josh H’s office. Mantis gives Bunch the Don Johnson mullet wig. We are still disguised as Village People. We discuss with the front desk guard about getting in to see Josh Hawley’s office, but Sara at the office denies us entry. So we head up to the same level, then Manifester uses a portal to attempt to get into the office. First time, he accidentally opens portal outside the building entirely. Second time, he succeeds. We see into the office, see Josh Hawley scrambling with Eric Greitens. We head through the portal! Initiative: Hawley, Mantis, Templar, Manifester, Eric Greitens, Bunch Hawley jumps over his desk and rises with a shotgun that he fires at us, missing us. Screaming in the distance. Mantis asks Bunch where the papers are. He says “under the desk!” Mantis steps forward and picks up the desk. “Do I have it?” “No there must be a safe under the floor” Templar tells Hawley to drop the shotgun, but isn’t convincing enough. Manifester tries to mind blast Greitens who is heading for a civil war sword on the wall, but fails. Greitens grabs the sword, rushes over and swings on Mantis. 2 dmg Bunch points to the floor and guards himself, trying to stay out of the action. Hawley curses at us. Mantis swings desk at Hawley’s shotgun, smashing it out of his hands. It lands against the far wall. Templar walks up to Hawley and zipties his hands, who curses about Democrats and woke communists. Manifester mind blasts Greitens, who collapses. Manifester looks under carpet protector for chair and finds floor safe. “What’s the combination?” “Go to hell you democrats” Door to office opens and two heavily armored men with blaster rifles point guns at us. Mantis rips the door off the safe easily. In the safe: mummified hand, handgun, a simple-looking dagger, gold bars, and sheets of laminated paper. Templar points at armored men and says “Get out!” They lower rifles and back away. Manifester kicks Greitens in the kidneys as running by and flicking off Hawley on the way to the portal. 4 dmg. Mantis grabs the busted safe with contents and runs to the portal. We’re one floor down. Alarm goes off. Manifester opens a portal to get us out, but it’s going the wrong way 60 floors up in midair. Instead he disguises everyone as cleaning staff. Push the elevator button and stroll out. As we’re leaving the building, 24/7 and an armored superhero “Ladybug” are heading up in response to the scene. We show up at the jail. We get there and there’s a hole in an outer wall ~5 floors up. Mantis (motorcycle guy) flies Bunch (construction worker) up to the hole, releases him back to jail, and he slips back into the population. Now we have notes. Fiddler’s real name is Mike “Madman” Markham. [Mike Markum is real person who claimed to have built a time machine.] Has home addresses. Purpose of his device is to correspond with other dimensions, snag superbeings, and bring them to this dimension. (in safe: pearl handled gun, 4 bars of gold, a desiccated hand, and notes which were laminated)
